description: RFC 0002 migration ledger: stable IDs, dependency DAG, contract IDs, caller sets, phase/status, test selectors, and retirement conditions. Status changes require test evidence for the current revision; a hand-edited status does not pass a gate.

migrations.title: Record legacy build reproducibility and establish the headless editor test target/toolchain
migrations.blocked: A headless strict C++20 test target is established (unittests/hammertest/run_headless.sh) and builds+runs under gcc 16 and clang with -Wall -Wextra -Werror. Windows-target parity is now VERIFIED for the MFC-free core: all 19 strict suites cross-compile to native Windows PE (MinGW-w64 g++ 16.1.1, static) and pass under both Wine 11 and GE-Proton11-5, matching the Linux runs (tools/quality/parity_wine.py; evidence architecture/hammer_windows_parity.json; profile quality/profiles/windows-pe-wine.json). Remaining before retirement: a Waf-integrated target and R03 flag validation. The legacy MFC SHELL build stays out of scope on this host: MFC headers/libs require Visual Studio (only the mfc140 runtime DLL is present); MinGW cannot provide MFC.
retireWhen: Linux 64-bit headless editor test target builds and runs
Windows-target parity of the strict core is verified under Wine/Proton
the headless and parity targets are integrated into CI with validated final flags

migrations.title: Implement exhaustive responsibility/effect ownership and migration schemas with reproducibility and coverage checks
migrations.blocked: Coverage is partial (13/452 files). Exhaustive per-file/per-symbol classification and reproducibility checks remain before H0 exit.
retireWhen: every hammer source file resolves to exactly one owner
inventory coverage status is 'complete' and validates
unowned/ambiguous files fail validation in a negative fixture

migrations.title: Add editor lexical rules and exact baselines, preserving the loader freeze; add negative checker fixtures
migrations.blocked: HAM003 (native/toolkit tokens in strict roots) is installed lexically. HAM001/HAM002 target/link-graph and HAM005 transaction-authority checks require the resolved build graph and compiler-grounded increments.
retireWhen: strict roots exist and are lexically clean
HAM001/HAM002/HAM005 land with hermetic and compiler-grounded checks

migrations.title: Establish minimal VMF/geometry/selection characterization fixtures and a versioned semantic comparator
migrations.blocked: The versioned semantic comparator now exists (hammer::formats::CompareKeyValues over the VMF/keyvalues parser+writer) with a passing negative corpus (a permissive always-equal comparator is caught). Remaining: broaden fixtures toward the RFC minimum corpus (convex/invalid brushes, transforms, texture axes, displacements, overlays, instances, malformed/encoding cases) and add provenance records under unittests/hammertest/fixtures.
retireWhen: versioned comparator exists with a passing negative corpus
the RFC minimum characterization fixtures load in a headless test

migrations.title: Extract a bounded geometry operation and compile it without MFC/PCH; route existing callers through the shared owner
intentionalDifferences: SnapToGrid rejects a non-positive grid size (degenerate input) instead of dividing by it, as the legacy Snap() did. Documented in public/hammer/geometry/aabb.h and covered by test_aabb.cpp.
fidelityNotes: Characterization caught that legacy hammer_mathlib V_rint rounds halves AWAY from zero, not to even. SnapToGrid now routes through hammer::geometry::RoundHalfAwayFromZero (public/hammer/geometry/rounding.h + hammer/core/geometry/rounding.cpp), the single owner of that rule (DRY), instead of std::rint. test_rounding.cpp and the .5-boundary case in test_aabb.cpp pin the difference; a std::rint variant fails the suite (verified).

Confirmed against the REAL MSVC toolchain: the unmodified legacy hammer/boundbox.cpp compiled by cl 19.29 (VS2019 v142 with atlmfc) under Wine, linked with AxisAlignedBox, is byte-identical across UpdateBounds/center/size/ContainsPoint/IsIntersectingBox/IsInsideBox/IsValidBox/SnapToGrid(.5-boundary)/Rotate90; a mutant round-half-to-even provider is caught (exit 1). Evidence: architecture/hammer_legacy_parity.json.
migrations.note: Strict shared owner hammer::geometry::AxisAlignedBox is implemented in public/hammer/geometry/aabb.h + hammer/core/geometry/aabb.cpp, compiles headlessly without MFC/tier0/PCH under gcc and clang (-Werror), and passes the conformance oracle unittests/hammertest/geometry/test_aabb.cpp. The contract record geometry.aabb.v1 is recorded, and test_aabb_negative.cpp proves the oracle detects a deliberately-broken (closed-face) provider. Legacy hammer/BoundBox remains the sole LIVE authority; no dual mutable model exists. Advancing to 'extracted' requires routing BoundBox callers through the shared owner via a named Vector<->Vec3 boundary adapter (hammer.adapters.source/mfc).
retireWhen: BoundBox operations own their behavior in hammer.geometry
legacy callers route through the shared owner via the Vector<->Vec3 adapter
extracted target builds without UI/PCH/GPU dependencies

migrations.title: Establish the strict runtime scene-handle mechanism (generational, document-scoped, stale-reference-rejecting)
migrations.note: Strict hammer.scene mechanism. (1) NodeHandle (document+index+generation) + HandleTable: stale-after-free rejection, slot-reuse generation rejection, independent-document isolation. (2) SceneGraph: the RFC H1 mutation/query boundary -- handle-addressed nodes, validated reparent (cycle/self/foreign-document, atomic-on-failure), atomic subtree delete, two-document isolation. All headless under gcc and clang (-Werror); each invariant has a negative provider proving the oracle is not vacuous. Remaining toward extraction: migrating the legacy CMapClass/CMapWorld hierarchy onto this owner (needs the legacy build) and wiring document-close invalidation.
retireWhen: the legacy scene hierarchy is addressed through this graph/handles
no raw scene pointer is stored across an edit that can free the node
document-close invalidates all outstanding handles

migrations.title: Establish the independent document edit-transaction / history reference model
migrations.note: The RFC verification-strategy 'small independent document/history model'. Pins transaction/history semantics: no-op neutrality, redo-tail drop, monotonic revision across undo, and the subtle undo-to-saved-clears-modified rule (modified is driven by saved POSITION, not the revision counter). A revision-based negative provider proves the oracle catches the common mistake. This is a semantics oracle ahead of the full H3 application authority (which also needs H2 persistence and the reversible-change payloads); it is not yet the live editor history and does not replace CHistory.
retireWhen: the live edit-transaction owner adopts these semantics with reversible change records
H2 persistence exists so save-position maps to a real saved file
legacy CHistory is retired behind the transaction seam

migrations.title: Establish the transactional save orchestration and the file-store port
migrations.note: First use of the hammer.ports pattern: IFileStore (a genuine polymorphic contract) plus SaveDocument (temp-write + atomic rename). A failed temp write or commit preserves the prior file; a truncate-then-write negative provider is caught. Verified headless with an in-memory fault-injecting fake that implements the same port (no app singletons/backdoors). Remaining: a real POSIX file-store provider, autosave-to-recovery-path (must not advance the ordinary save position), and multi-file manifest save recovery.
retireWhen: a real file-store provider passes the same IFileStore contract suite
document save routes through SaveDocument with autosave/recovery and manifest cases
legacy in-place save paths are retired

migrations.title: Integrate the headless reference workflow (EditorDocument): open/edit/undo/redo/save/reopen/compare
migrations.note: The RFC 'executable headless reference workflow' now runs end-to-end, composing hammer.formats (VMF codec + comparator), DocumentHistory (one history authority; snapshot-based undo), and SaveDocument over the IFileStore port. Verified: detached load, one-edit-one-history-unit, no-op neutrality, undo restores recorded content, undo-to-saved clears modified, save advances the saved position, and save->reopen semantic equality. A non-restoring-undo negative provider is caught. Content is a keyvalues tree for this slice; typed scene content (NodeHandle-addressed brushes/faces via hammer.scene), selection integration, and the MFC/GTK presenter adapters are the next steps -- the presenter adapters need the legacy build / GTK host.
retireWhen: typed scene content replaces the keyvalues-tree document model
selection and transform edits route through this document's transaction authority
the workflow runs through the MFC and GTK presenter adapters

migrations.title: Introduce the per-document application seam and explicit state ownership; pass two-document independence tests
retireWhen: EditorSession owns per-document application services
two independent documents pass isolation tests
scene objects no longer borrow a CDocument

migrations.title: Move property-draft commit policy out of selection; execute selection/property/transform migration
migrations.note: Two foundational pieces landed in hammer.app, both headless-verified under gcc and clang with negative providers. (1) hammer::app::PropertyValue owns the RFC empty-vs-unset-vs-mixed multi-selection distinction. (2) The shared ENTITY EDITOR: hammer::app::EntitySelection (public/hammer/app/entity_selection.h + hammer/core/app/entity_selection.cpp) plus EditorDocument::EntityCount/EntityName/EntityClassName/AggregateProperty/SetPropertyOnSelection wire PropertyValue into live use over a document's entities and give an ATOMIC multi-entity edit (one undo unit; sensitivity suite catches a non-atomic per-entity editor). The thin GTK sibling (hammer.adapters.gtk) now drives entity selection + property editing entirely through this authority (builds to a real ELF via build_gtk_shell.sh; the delegated workflow is verified headlessly by test_shell_workflow.cpp), so GTK and its MFC sibling share ONE entity editor logic. Contract app.entity_editor.v1. Remaining for this worked migration: the property-draft commit policy (commit-valid/report-invalid/discard), a selection set over scene handles (currently indices), the transform request, and routing legacy CSelection/property-sheet callers -- which needs the legacy build.
retireWhen: all selection entry points route through the application policy
no property-sheet access remains in extracted selection code
menu/keyboard/tool paths share one edit operation

migrations.title: Run R1 renderer bridge feasibility; record dependencies and measurements
migrations.blocked: Requires the H0 minimal render contract and the selected GTK4/libadwaita X11/Wayland profile before the spike can measure context/target ownership, resize, scale, capture, and shutdown.
retireWhen: one real Source-material viewport renders in a GTK host on the selected profiles
bridge approach (in-context vs offscreen share) is chosen with measurements

migrations.title: Establish the Source Vector<->Vec3 / BoundBox<->AxisAlignedBox boundary seam that both UI siblings share
migrations.note: The single named owner (DRY) of the Source Vector<->Vec3 and BoundBox<->AxisAlignedBox conversion policy: hammer/adapters/source/vector_interop.h. This is the non-strict seam the thin UI siblings hammer.adapters.mfc and hammer.adapters.gtk both stand on to drive the reusable geometry library on Source's own data. It deliberately depends on the Source platform layer (mathlib/vector.h, boundbox.h), which the strict libraries never may, so its conformance suite runs on the MSVC/Wine parity lane, not linux-headless-core.
fidelityNotes: Substitution guarantee proven under the REAL MSVC toolchain (cl 19.29 under Wine): for the unmodified legacy BoundBox, running a reusable geometry op directly equals ToAABB->op->FromAABB for SnapToGrid(16 .5-boundary), SnapToGrid(8), and Rotate90 on all axes, plus exact Vector<->Vec3 round-trip. A y/z-swap BuggyAdapter is caught by 9 clauses (oracle sound). Evidence: architecture/hammer_legacy_parity.json (adapters section); driver scratchpad legacy-parity/run_adapter_parity.sh.
migrations.note2: This seam is the enabling dependency for advancing HAM-GEOMETRY-001 from 'characterized' to 'cutover': live BoundBox callers can now delegate geometry to hammer::geometry through this adapter. The adapter is permanent sibling infrastructure and is not itself retired.

migrations.title: Extract the reusable core of the MFC CUpdateHint document-change aggregation onto the strict geometry+scene libraries
migrations.note: hammer::app::UpdateHint (public/hammer/app/update_hint.h + hammer/core/app/update_hint.cpp) is the reusable aggregation model both UI siblings need: notify-code-bucketed changed nodes (hammer::scene::NodeHandle) + a unioned affected region (hammer::geometry::AxisAlignedBox), with the legacy kMaxNotifyCodes=16 capacity preserved. It composes the two already-extracted strict libraries and builds headlessly (no MFC/tier0/PCH). Verified on 4 lanes: gcc, clang, and MinGW-w64 PE under both Wine (architecture/hammer_windows_parity.json, 23/23).
fidelityNotes: The legacy hammer/updatehint.cpp is ORPHANED DEAD CODE: it is in no .vpc build project and does not compile (unbalanced parens at line 128; references to non-members m_Objects/nIndex). There is no live behavior to byte-match, so this is a faithful reconstruction of the intent in hammer/updatehint.h (NotifyList_t[MAX_NOTIFY_CODES] buckets, m_nListEntries, m_UpdateRegion), rebuilt on the strict libraries. Classified evidenceKind=decision, not observed. The negative suite proves the oracle pins the capacity clause the legacy MAX_NOTIFY_CODES guarded.
retireWhen: live document-mutation/view-update callers route change aggregation through hammer::app::UpdateHint via the MFC adapter shell
the orphaned hammer/updatehint.cpp and hammer/UpdateHint.h are removed

migrations.title: Provide the first real IFileStore provider (disk-backed) so the reusable app libraries can persist without a filesystem dependency of their own
migrations.note: hammer::adapters::platform::DiskFileStore is the first production hammer::ports::IFileStore provider (previously only the in-memory test fake existed). Atomic Write via temp-file+rename. A shared IFileStore conformance suite now runs against the real store, the fake, and a broken provider (ports.file_store.v1), proving substitutability and oracle soundness on gcc, clang, and MinGW PE under Wine.
retireWhen: a platform capability provider supersedes it
all editor persistence routes through IFileStore providers only

migrations.title: Stand up the thin GTK4/libadwaita UI sibling on the reusable editor libraries
migrations.note: hammer/adapters/gtk/hammer_gtk_shell.cpp is the actual thin GTK sibling: a libadwaita AdwApplicationWindow whose every action delegates to hammer::app::EditorDocument persisted through DiskFileStore; it holds no editor logic. It COMPILES and LINKS to a real ELF binary against gtk4 4.22 + libadwaita 1.9 + the reusable libraries and nothing else (unittests/hammertest/adapters/build_gtk_shell.sh). Its delegated New/SetKey/Save/Open/Undo/Redo workflow is verified headlessly (adapters.gtk_shell.v1, test_shell_workflow.cpp) since a GUI needs a display. This is the sibling architecture realized end-to-end for one shell; the MFC sibling drives the same libraries.
retireWhen: the GTK shell reaches declared H5 editor parity
superseded shell/glue removed at H7

migrations.title: Stand up the thin MFC UI sibling on the reusable editor libraries (new shell, not the legacy engine-bound one)
migrations.note: hammer/adapters/mfc/hammer_mfc_shell.cpp is the thin MFC sibling of the GTK shell: a CWinApp/CFrameWnd whose command handlers delegate to hammer::app::EditorDocument persisted through DiskFileStore; no editor policy. Built NEW (not the legacy engine-bound Hammer shell), so it depends only on MFC + the reusable libraries and BUILDS to a real PE32+ GUI exe with the real MSVC+MFC toolchain (cl 19.29, atlmfc), and its delegated New/SetKey/Save/Open/Undo/Redo workflow RUNS under Wine (test_mfc_workflow.cpp, exit 0). This is the key realization that the MFC sibling does NOT require the D2 whole-Source-engine link. Evidence: architecture/hammer_mfc_parity.json; repro unittests/hammertest/adapters/build_mfc_shell.sh. Local gate (MSVC+MFC toolchain not in CI).
retireWhen: the MFC sibling reaches declared H5 editor parity
superseded shell/glue removed at H7

migrations.title: Implement VMF displacement (dispinfo) geometry as a strict headless module: keyvalues parse + subdivided bilinear surface
migrations.note: The brush contract (geometry.brush.v1) deliberately excludes displacements as a later migration; this is that migration's core. New strict headless geometry (no legacy source, authority=new): hammer::formats::ParseDispInfo (public/hammer/formats/vmf_geometry.h, hammer/core/formats/vmf_geometry.cpp; moved out of hammer.geometry on 2026-09-25 so geometry has no formats dependency) decodes a VMF dispinfo block into a geometry::DispInfo, and hammer::geometry::BuildDisplacementSurface produces the (2^power+1)^2 vertex grid + 2*(side-1)^2 triangles, with base = bilinear interpolation of the face's four corners (grid origin = the corner nearest startposition, matching VBSP/Hammer), then per-vertex offset + normal*distance + faceNormal*elevation. Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance unittests/hammertest/geometry/test_displacement.cpp checks grid sizes (powers 2-4), flat bilinear identity, uniform push, and startposition orientation; test_displacement_negative.cpp proves ParseDispInfo rejects a bad power, a wrong-length row, a missing row, and an absent normals grid. Also parses alphas (per-vertex blend, surfaced as DisplacementSurface.vertexAlphas), subdiv, and triangle_tags (validated grids). Not yet consumed by the scene/render bridge (that wiring is source-engine-3c's scene/render seam), and offset_normals/allowed_verts plus subdiv smoothing / alpha+tag rendering are later increments.
retireWhen: a later displacement increment supersedes it with alphas/triangle_tags/subdiv/allowed_verts support
displaced faces render through this surface in the scene/render bridge

migrations.title: Implement func_instance expansion: load nested VMFs via IFileStore, transform (QAngle rotate + translate) and merge world solids/entities, flatten the tree
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new) over the keyvalues codec (hammer.formats), the IFileStore port (hammer.ports), and geometry Vec3d. hammer::formats::ExpandInstances loads each func_instance's referenced VMF through the store, transforms its world solids (each side plane's three points) and entities (origin) by the Source QAngle rotation + origin translation, composes nested placements as a matrix product ((R*Ri)*p + (R*oi + o)), and returns a flattened document with no func_instance entities. Recursion is bounded by maxDepth so a self/cyclic reference is a reported error, not a loop. Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_instancing.cpp checks translate/yaw/nested composition + instance removal, test_instancing_negative.cpp proves missing-file/cyclic/no-file are errors while a good instance expands. Declared limits: texture-axis rotation, entity angle composition, $fixup/replace variables, and instance visgroup/group merging are later increments.
retireWhen: a later increment adds texture-axis rotation, entity angle composition, and $fixup variable substitution
the editor's collapse-instance command and map compile consume this expansion

migrations.title: Implement the FGD entity-schema parser: class kinds, typed key properties, choices/flags, and base() inheritance resolution
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new), self-contained tokenizer + recursive-descent parser (C++ stdlib only). hammer::formats::ParseFgd reads @PointClass/@SolidClass/@BaseClass/@KeyValueClass/@NPCClass/@FilterClass/@MoveClass declarations, base(...) inheritance, typed key properties (string/integer/float/choices/flags/target_source/angle/...), defaults, and choices/flags value lists; unknown top-level directives (@mapsize/@include/@MaterialExclusion/@AutoVisGroup) are skipped, not errors. ResolveClass flattens inheritance (base-first, child overrides, cycle-guarded). This is the entity schema the property editor consumes. Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_fgd.cpp checks kinds/typed-properties/choices/flags/empty-fields/inheritance, test_fgd_negative.cpp proves missing-type, unterminated-body, missing-name, and stray-token error out while a good FGD parses. Declared limits: input/output declarations are parsed but not stored, non-base helper metadata (size/color/iconsprite/studio) is ignored, and @include is not resolved (referenced file not loaded).
retireWhen: a later increment stores I/O (input/output) definitions and resolves @include
the entity property editor consumes this schema for authored-key validation

migrations.title: Implement cordon filtering: keep only world solids/entities whose bounds intersect a cordon box for partial compile/export
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new) over the keyvalues codec + geometry Vec3d. hammer::formats::ApplyCordon returns a VMF filtered to a CordonBox: a world solid is kept iff its AABB (union of side-plane points) intersects the box (inclusive edges); a point entity iff its origin is inside; a brush entity iff any of its solids intersect; a positionless entity always. An inverted (mins>maxs) box removes all positional geometry. Non-world/entity blocks are preserved verbatim. Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_cordon.cpp checks inside/outside/straddling/edge-touching + entity rules + metadata preservation, test_cordon_negative.cpp proves discrimination (universe keeps all, empty/far removes all) so a constant keep-all/remove-all impl is caught. Declared limits: brush-bounds intersection (not exact hull-vs-box clipping) and no boundary splitting of solids.
retireWhen: a later increment adds exact hull-vs-box clipping and cordon-boundary solid splitting
the partial-compile/export path consumes this filter

migrations.title: Implement info_overlay parsing + world-quad projection so decal overlays render on brush faces
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new) over the keyvalues codec + geometry Vec3d. hammer::formats::ParseOverlay reads an info_overlay entity (material, sides face-id list, BasisOrigin/U/V/Normal, uv0..uv3 corners, StartU/EndU/StartV/EndV) and WorldCorners() projects the four corners to world space (BasisOrigin + BasisU*uv.x + BasisV*uv.y + BasisNormal*uv.z); ExtractOverlays pulls every valid overlay from a document. Missing material/sides/basis/corner or a non-info_overlay yields nullopt (no partial overlay). Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_overlay.cpp checks parse + projected corner positions + non-overlay skip, test_overlay_negative.cpp proves the required-field rejections. Declared limits: no quad-to-face clipping, no material rendering, no info_overlay_transition (water) support.
retireWhen: a later increment clips the overlay quad to its target faces and handles info_overlay_transition
the renderer draws overlays from this projection

migrations.title: Implement VisGroup tree parsing + visibility filtering (hide a parent hides descendant members) for the VisGroup panel
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new) over the keyvalues codec. hammer::formats::ParseVisGroups builds the nested visgroup tree from the top-level visgroups block; ApplyVisGroupFilter removes every world solid/entity whose editor.visgroupid membership falls in the hidden set, expanded down the tree so hiding a parent hides descendant-group members. Objects with no (or non-numeric) membership stay; non-world/entity blocks preserved. Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_visgroups.cpp checks tree parse + hide-parent/leaf + empty-keeps-all + counts, test_visgroups_negative.cpp pins descendant expansion, empty/unknown keep-all, and non-numeric-membership handling (the properties a naive filter gets wrong). Declared limits: no group-block (object grouping) membership, no persisted visgroupshown flags, no auto-visgroups.
retireWhen: a later increment adds group-block membership, persisted visgroupshown flags, and auto-visgroups
the VisGroup panel drives visibility through this filter

migrations.title: Implement the VMT material-definition parser (shader + parameters + proxy/patch detection) as the single DRY VMT parser
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new) over the keyvalues codec. hammer::formats::ParseMaterial reads a VMT definition: shader = first top-level block name, parameters = its pairs, hasProxies flags a Proxies sub-block; Param/HasParam are case-insensitive, BaseTexture()/SurfaceProp() are convenience accessors, IsPatch() detects the patch shader. Definition-only: no VTF pixels, no rendering. This is the single DRY VMT parser: source-engine-87's material_catalog (VPK/texture loading) consumes THIS Material/ParseMaterial rather than a second parser (a prior duplicate material.cpp was reconciled to this one). Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_material.cpp checks shader/params/accessors/case-insensitivity/proxy/patch, test_material_negative.cpp proves empty/whitespace/unterminated are rejected. Declared limits: patch include/replace not resolved (replace/insert child blocks not exposed as params), no VTF decode.
retireWhen: a later increment resolves patch include/replace and exposes replace/insert parameters
the material catalog and renderer consume this definition parser

migrations.title: Implement object-group resolution: parse group hierarchy + expand a selection to top-level group siblings
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new) over the keyvalues codec. hammer::formats::ParseGroups builds a GroupTable (solid->group, group->parent) from world group/solid editor.groupid; TopLevelGroupOfSolid follows the parent chain (cycle-guarded); ExpandGroupSelection expands selected solid ids to every solid sharing a top-level group, so a member of a nested sub-group selects the whole top-level group while ungrouped solids stay singular. Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_groups.cpp checks nested top-level resolution + selection expansion + multi-select union, test_groups_negative.cpp pins nested top-level expansion, ungrouped singularity, and cyclic-chain termination. Declared limits: world-solid group membership only (no entity group membership), no create/dissolve/persist group edits.
retireWhen: a later increment expands entity group membership and persists group create/dissolve edits
the selection tool drives group-select through this resolver

migrations.title: Implement prefab instantiation (place a VMF fragment by origin/angles) on the shared VMF transform owner
migrations.note: New strict headless module (authority=new). hammer::formats::InstantiatePrefab places a parsed VMF fragment at a Placement (origin + Source QAngle), returning transformed world solids + entities. It builds on the NEW shared transform owner hammer/formats/vmf_transform (Mat3/AngleMatrix/Multiply/Rotate/Place/TransformSolid/TransformEntity), which was EXTRACTED from instancing.cpp so func_instance and prefab share ONE QAngle placement implementation (DRY) instead of duplicating the rotation matrix + plane/origin math; instancing.cpp was refactored to use it and its suites still pass (its manifest sources now include vmf_transform.cpp). Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_prefab.cpp checks translate/yaw placement + count preservation, test_prefab_negative.cpp pins placement-applied, identity-preserved, and count preservation. Declared limits: entity-angle composition + texture-axis rotation are shared vmf_transform limits; no on-disk prefab library or id-remap on merge.
retireWhen: a later increment adds entity-angle composition, texture-axis rotation, and id-remap on merge
the prefab library/insert tool consumes this instantiation

migrations.title: Compose the map export/compile-prep pipeline (expand instances -> drop hidden visgroups -> clip cordon) over the format cores
migrations.note: New strict headless COMPOSITION (authority=new): hammer::formats::PrepareForCompile turns an authored VMF into compile-ready geometry by ordering the single-purpose cores -- (1) ExpandInstances (flatten func_instances via IFileStore), (2) ApplyVisGroupFilter (drop hidden-visgroup objects), (3) optional ApplyCordon (partial-compile clip). It adds NO new transform/intersection logic (DRY); it only orders instancing+visgroups+cordon and returns counts. A failed stage (bad func_instance) aborts with a diagnostic, no silent partial. This is the headless entry point behind the shell's Run Map/Export. Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_map_export.cpp checks instance-expand + visgroup-drop + cordon-clip compose with correct survivors, test_map_export_negative.cpp proves stage-failure propagation. Declared limits: no BSP/VIS/RAD or external compiler invocation, no material resolution, cordon-boundary splitting is the cordon core's limit.
retireWhen: a later increment invokes the external compiler toolchain and resolves materials for export
the shell's Run Map/Export path consumes this pipeline

migrations.title: Build the entity property-sheet row model (FGD schema + entity keyvalues -> property grid rows) for the entity editor UI
migrations.note: New strict headless model (authority=new) composing formats.fgd (ResolveClass) + the keyvalues codec. hammer::formats::BuildPropertySheet turns (entity block, FGD class table) into the property-grid row model an entity property-sheet widget renders: schema rows first (resolved FGD class, base-first, declaration order) each carrying type/display/choices and the entity value or the FGD default (isSet reflects whether the entity set it, case-insensitive match), then extra non-schema entity keys, with classname/id/editor excluded. This is the HEADLESS MODEL behind the FGD-driven entity property sheet UI (the widget only renders these rows; the GTK/MFC widget wiring is the shell owner's, source-engine-3c). Compiles headlessly under g++ and clang (-Werror); conformance test_entity_property_sheet.cpp checks inherited/default/choices/extra/meta, test_entity_property_sheet_negative.cpp pins unset-rows-show-defaults + meta exclusion + no spurious rows. Declared limits: does not write edits back, validate values by type, resolve I/O, or group rows into smartedit categories.
retireWhen: a later increment writes edited values back through the app/history layer and groups smartedit categories
the shell's entity property-sheet widget renders this model
